subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the parabola passing through the points (−2, 1), (1, 2), (−1, 3) and having its axis parallel to the x-axis.

mark_split.label: Set up the general equation and substitute the three points
Eliminate n to get two equations in l and m
Substitute back for n and write the final equation

steps.label: Set up the general equation
steps.margin_note: First two marks, for the correct general form and all three substitutions.
lines: The equation of a parabola with axis parallel to the x-axis is x = ly² + my + n.
steps.why: An axis parallel to the x-axis means y is the free variable and x is written in terms of y², so the general equation has y² and y in place of the usual x² and x — three unknowns l, m, n need three points, which is exactly what is given.
common_mistakes: Writing the general form as y = lx² + mx + n, the axis-parallel-to-y-axis case instead.
Substituting a point's x and y into the wrong side of the equation.
steps.memory_tip: Axis along x means x is written in terms of y — x = ly² + my + n, the mirror image of the more familiar y = lx² + mx + n.

steps.label: Eliminate n
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Watch the signs carefully — every right-hand side has a −(−2) to simplify first.
steps.why: Subtracting equation (1) from the other two removes n immediately, and leaves a pair of equations in only l and m.
common_mistakes: Losing the negative sign inside −(−2) while simplifying the right-hand side.
Forgetting that (1) has to be subtracted from BOTH (2) and (3), not just one of them.
steps.memory_tip: Subtract equation (1) from the other two and n cancels every time, since every equation has the same +n.

steps.label: Solve for l and m
steps.margin_note: Two marks for both l and m — check them by putting both back into (4): 3(−5/2) + 21/2 should give 3.
steps.why: With m written in terms of l from (4), substituting into (5) leaves one equation in the single unknown l.
common_mistakes: Substituting m = 3 − 3l into (4) instead of (5), which just restates (4) and gives no new information.
Losing the negative sign on l = −5/2 partway through.
steps.memory_tip: Write m in terms of l from the shorter equation, then substitute into the other one.

steps.label: Write the final equation
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Check the boxed equation with one of the three given points — it should give 0.
lines: Substitute l = −5/2, m = 21/2, n = −10 in x = ly² + my + n:
steps.why: Multiplying through by 2, the shared denominator of every fraction here, clears them all in one move and leaves a whole-number equation.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only some of the terms by 2 and leaving a mixed equation.
Writing the boxed equation with a wrong sign on the y term.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply through by 2, the shared denominator of every fraction here, to reach one whole-number equation.

insider_note: Every coefficient here was checked by substituting all three given points back into the boxed equation — each gives exactly 0, which is the fastest way to catch an arithmetic slip in this kind of question.
